key_insight: SANA-Video 2.0 shows that high-quality video generation can be scaled efficiently with a hybrid attention design, reaching up to 720p on a single GPU. It matches full-softmax video transformers while preserving the linear-scaling benefits needed for long sequences.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the compute and memory bottleneck of video diffusion transformers, where full softmax attention becomes too expensive for long, high-resolution video generation.
method: Introduces a unified hybrid video diffusion transformer at 5B and 14B parameter scales.
Uses Hybrid Linear-Softmax Attention: gated linear attention for efficient O(N)-style token mixing plus periodic gated-softmax anchor layers to recover global attention quality.
Designs the model to generate high-quality videos up to 720p on a single GPU without relying on quadratic attention throughout.
impact: This matters because it makes high-resolution video generation more practical and accessible on limited hardware. For practitioners, it offers a path to scale video models without the prohibitive cost of standard full-attention transformers.

paper_title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
paper_authors: Junsong Chen, Jincheng Yu, Yitong Li, Shuchen Xue, Haozhe Liu
